title: My experience with travel eSIMs in Bali
body:
O.P.
this post was edited
I spent a week on Bali earlier this month, and decided to try 4 different eSIMs, all around the Seminyak area
The companies were Holafly, Airalo, Saily and Bytesim.
The exit country on all of these is Singapore except one
Airalo: this sat on the 3 network, recently merged with Indosat but these 2 run seperate networks.
Interestingly the Asia esim says it uses telkomsel so next year I’ll try this. The Asia profile uses different carriers to the country specific sim for almost every country on the list
I liked Airalo here. 4G only unfortunately but always very consistent particularly with the uploads. Always around 15-20 down, 15-20 up. In the app it does promise a 5G connection, the only problem though is that 3 only appears to have one 5G cell in all of Denpasar if you look at their coverage map, so in that sense I didn’t feel like I was lied to. Trying to select indosat manually would latch on but won’t get a data connection before falling back to 3
The only thing was in certain parts of Seminyak, just walking along the beach road outdoors, video calls would drop out and that was a problem for me as a family member wanted to see around the area and some of the hotels. A tiny beachside cafe we loved had the poor signal problem so I couldn’t hotspot my phone there. It’s a few plastic chairs around a wooden table on the beach and one guy with his tiny kitchen behind the beach but we loved it. Wifi? If you ask him he’ll hotspot his phone which feels cruel considering how poor they are. Takes card payment too. Anyway:
The only other negative here is 3 has heavy congestion in ubud. I was there on a day trip and this was bad. Less than 1mbps down if Speedtest ran at all.
Maybe it’s great at 6am but If I was basing myself st ubud I wouldn’t buy Airalo. This was despite having good signal too
Next is Holafly. Much faster, used telkomsel 5G but exit node was USA (Texas IIRC). No dramas with signal here but yes the latency was significant. Surprisingly though, no issues with video calls the delay was barely noticeable. I’d be happy to use it but as a geek I prefer my local sim to use a different carrier to my roaming sim from Australia. Speeds were great, 200+ no worries
Next is Saily. This was a bit more expensive but provided more. Network side ad blocking and you select your own virtual location in the app. Using Australia didn’t have much more latency than no virtual location and less latency than using NordVPN to Australia from my phone so it’s all done server side (Saily own NordVPN so that virtual location is definitely network side)
Overall this had by far the best speeds and connection quality. I even saw 400mbps down. This used XL but I also saw telkomsel in use too at times.
That price though. $48 USD / 70 AUD for 15 days unlimited – ouch! I only had it for 5 days just to try it. It’s 5GB/day and exceeding that drops you back to 1mbps. The fixed data packages offer better value here. Saily is always a positive quality experience though, I had a fixed data plan with them in Canada last year and it was terrific. Best for privacy too as you can just select whichever virtual location in the app
Finally we have ByteSIM. No prizes for guessing who they resell because a Singtel esim lands on your phone. Here I could finally choose among 3 networks but it preferred XL. This wasn’t great and i probably wouldn’t buy it again. It would randomly lose data connection as it searches for the best network. Best for you? No don’t be silly, best for Singtels accountants I think.
After sone very fast speeds initially it just randomly throttled me down to 5mbps. I thought ok maybe it will be back to full tilt tomorrow but no still 5mbps. Latency was great sometimes but over 200ms other times. The page selling this esim promises guaranteed 1080p video streaming even when fair use policy has been exceeded. I’m sure that’s true
I really like eSIMs. Yes you pay more, especially in a country like Indonesia, but there is no line up, no scanning your passport or having some random take photos of your passport on their phone (yes I’ve had this, right in front of me too), no KYC, ID checks or IMEI registration of your phone (nobody knows where this data is stored, who it’s shared with or how long it’s kept for) and it’s available the second I land. In theory, you should drop to other networks where the preferred network isn’t available too.
Yes there is cheaper eSIMs for Indonesia but they all have some weird catch when you drill down into it and look at it more. I prefer companies that are upfront about what networks they use, what exit node they have and how much data per day is allowed on an “unlimited “ sim before you run into slower speeds and what that speed is.

TheDoc writes...
Singtel. 500GB. A$6
Thank you but there’s 2 problems there 1) you have to arrive in Singapore at some point in the use or else it’s data only and 4G only (it’s in the ts&cs) 2) it’s not clear how to get it for that price, however the regular price of $12 SGD is still cheap enough 3) you still have to register your passport with Singtel
Also I was just posting my experience using these companies. These are all very popular, easy to use options
[User #682531821 postsWestsurfWhirlpool Enthusiast] Why wouldn’t you just use an online Indonesian eSIM provider like BaliSIM?
Cheaper and with local support. Better than buying at airport. Most plans are 30 days. IMEI is guaranteed connection for 90 days with Xl Avita or if you decide on Telekomsel register IMEI with customs at airport to ensure 90 day connectivity.

[User #55247622912 postspedrovyes, I changed it....Whirlpool Forums Addict] I today bought the tourist esim via XL online directly. I had QRIS payment wallet already (DANA is fairly straightforward to add some funds to). XL website had some ID requirements, as they provide calls allowance also, but it was easy enough to process online myself. Prefer to upload it directly myself on the company website vs a middle man random person trying to handle it over photos/whastapp.
14GB for 30 days. Cost was Rp46,000 (just under $4 AUD).
